card.name: Inside foreign names and Dutch words
card.fires_on: Word endings partway through non-English words, such as the Dutch verb dimmen, Slovene or Slavic place and person names, and the drug name NULOJIX. It fires on the piece after the stem, such as men, nas, en, an, j or J.

modes.label: Dutch word endings
modes.description: Ending of Dutch words such as dimmen, or of the adjective grooten, in Dutch text.
modes.example: You may see the following phrase a lot: "Effe dim<<men>>!" ("Cool it!").

modes.label: Slavic and other names
modes.description: Closing piece of a rare place or person name, often Slovene or Croatian, or Icelandic.
modes.example: Etimološki slovar slovenskih zemljepisnih imen. Ljubljana: Modrij<<an>> and Založba ZRC,

modes.label: Drug brand name
modes.description: A letter inside a rare brand name in a drug label.
modes.example: NULO<<J>>IX is for intravenous infusion only.

card.writes: Promoted and suppressed tokens are a mix of odd word pieces and Chinese words, so there is no clear output effect.
card.plain: It lights up on the later pieces of unusual foreign names and Dutch words that the model has to split up.
